text: Unimodularity means M=Mᵛ. The correspondence sends Mᵛ/L to (M/L)⊥, so equality is equivalent to H=H⊥, as in [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). Lean uses the bilinear Lagrangian condition and assumes integrality and nondegeneracy; evenness is not inferred for an odd overlattice. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L170) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L255) passes.
Duality corresponds to orthogonal complement.
Unimodularity is literal equality with the dual carrier.

The constructed lattice retains carrier M and the original form, so its defining unimodularity equation is exactly M=Mᵛ. This agrees with the dual-lattice convention of [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). The result compares actual embedded carriers; it does not replace equality by an abstract isomorphism. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L158) passes.
The constructed lattice has the same dual submodule.

The carrier consists of vectors pairing integrally with every element of M. Since L⊆M, it lies in Lᵛ; symmetry and M⊆Lᵛ show it contains L. Thus it is again intermediate, as in the dual chain of [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). This construction itself requires no nondegeneracy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L103) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L110) passes.
The dual of L is the top carrier Lᵛ.
Under nondegeneracy the dual of Lᵛ returns L.

The order correspondence is injective and takes Mᵛ to H⊥. Therefore Mᵛ=M exactly when H=H⊥, the bilinear Lagrangian condition in [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). Such equality also implies integrality of M. No quadratic-isotropy or evenness claim is hidden in the carrier-level statement. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L170) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L127) passes.
The dual carrier gives the orthogonal-complement subgroup.
Self-duality in particular forces integrality.

Packaging an integral intermediate carrier as a lattice preserves its carrier and ambient form. Its dual is therefore exactly L.form.dualSubmodule(M), the carrier of dual M. This agrees with the common-ambient dual construction in [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8), not an independently chosen abstract dual. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L165) passes.
The resulting dual is contained in the original dual carrier.

A class represented by x belongs to Mᵛ/L exactly when B(x,m) is integral for every m∈M, equivalently its discriminant pairing with every class of M/L is zero. This is the orthogonal-complement identity of [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8); nondegeneracy supplies the finite bilinear module used in Lean. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L135) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L281) passes.
The representative criterion tests the entire subgroup.
The inverse-image formulation gives the same dual carrier.

Forgetting interval-membership proofs leaves exactly the dual submodule of M for the fixed ambient form. This is the embedded dual used in [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). The formula remains meaningful for a degenerate form and does not itself assert double duality. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L135) passes.
The dual submodule has the expected integral-pairing criterion on quotient representatives.

The quotient pairing is B(x,y) modulo ℤ, so vanishing against all classes from M/L means integral pairing with all of M. This gives precisely membership in Mᵛ/L, as in [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). The argument works before nondegeneracy and makes no finiteness assertion. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Bilinear.lean#L108) passes.
Pairing zero in ℚ/ℤ is exactly integrality of the ambient pairing.

Every vector pairing integrally with M pairs integrally with its submodule L, so Mᵛ⊆Lᵛ. This is the reversed dual inclusion in [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). The constructed lattice keeps the common form, which is essential to comparing these two dual carriers. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L158) passes.
The lattice dual is the same intermediate dual carrier.

The map includes Mᵛ into Lᵛ and takes its class modulo L, giving an ℤ-linear map to A_L. This is the subgroup embedding Mᵛ/L⊆A_L in [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). The declaration’s domain is Mᵛ itself; it is not claimed injective before quotienting by L. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L190) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L195) passes.
The map uses the same ambient representative modulo L.
Its values lie in the annihilator of M/L.

Evaluation takes y∈Mᵛ to the class of the identical ambient vector in Lᵛ/L, with the inclusion proof supplied by reversed dual containment. This is the map underlying [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). It does not reduce modulo M or change representatives through an arbitrary equivalence. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L195) passes.
The displayed class annihilates every class from M/L.

A vector y∈Mᵛ pairs integrally with every m∈M. Its class modulo L therefore annihilates H=M/L under the discriminant pairing, exactly the inclusion in [Nikulin Proposition 1.4.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). Orthogonality is to the entire subgroup; testing only the self-pairing would not suffice. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Dual.lean#L135) passes.
Dual-subgroup membership is equivalent to vanishing against all of H.

This is explicitly the image I/(I∩m²) in m/m², m=ker ε, as obtained from [Mathlib’s cotangent map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean#L182). Since I⊆m, cotangentMap takes each defining equation to its first-order class. [The kernel identification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L207) checks this image interpretation; it does not identify the possibly larger conormal-module fiber I/mI.
The quotient cotangent map has precisely the declared conormal image as its kernel.

Membership means exactly that a cotangent vector is represented by some y∈I. This unfolds the submodule image, with no arbitrary choice of representative affecting the condition, consistently with [Mathlib’s cotangent map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean#L182). [The quotient-class formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L134) checks that such representatives map to zero in the subgroup cotangent space.
The map sends an augmentation representative to its quotient augmentation class.

If I≤J, mapping both ideals into the same m/m² gives N*(I)≤N*(J). This is image monotonicity in [Mathlib’s cotangent map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean#L182); geometrically the smaller subgroup has more first-order equations. [The Lie-dimension comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L423) checks the reversed subgroup direction in the finite-dimensional field specialization.
Larger defining ideals give no larger tangent dimension under finite ambient cotangents.

The quotient bialgebra map induces m/m²→m̄/m̄² in the coordinate-map direction, exactly [Mathlib’s cotangent map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean#L182). Its dual will point from subgroup tangents into ambient tangents. [The displacement equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L126) and [surjectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L196) check the intended map over arbitrary commutative rings, without flatness or smoothness.
The quotient cotangent map commutes with displacement x−ε(x) for arbitrary x.
Every quotient augmentation cotangent class lifts, with no flatness or smoothness.

For every x∈H, the map takes the class of x−ε(x) to the corresponding displacement of q(x). Counit compatibility makes this the natural cotangent map of [Mathlib’s cotangent map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean#L182). [The augmentation-representative formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L134) checks the specialization; x itself need not belong to the augmentation ideal.
The map sends an augmentation representative to its quotient augmentation class.

The class of x∈m maps to the class of q(x)∈m̄, with the target membership justified by preservation of counits. This is [Mathlib’s cotangent map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean#L182) on ideal representatives. [The duality equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L152) checks that the resulting map is exactly dual to the closed-subgroup differential.
Cotangent duality identifies precomposition by the quotient cotangent map with the subgroup differential.

Turning f:m̄/m̄²→B into a counit-valued derivation and then restricting along q equals first composing f with the cotangent map. This is the natural derivation/cotangent correspondence in [Milne, 10.6 and Proposition 10.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=199). [The differential’s evaluation formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Tangent.lean#L107) checks direction and coefficient transport; no finite-projectivity or field assumption is needed.
The subgroup differential evaluates a derivation on the coordinate quotient, with the correct coefficient transport.

Every augmentation element of H/I lifts to one of H, since the quotient preserves counits and I⊆ker ε. Hence the induced cotangent map is onto, as in [Stacks, Lemma 29.33.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01UZ). [Its kernel formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L207) checks the complete short exact sequence with the defined image submodule. No smoothness or flatness is required.
The quotient cotangent map has precisely the declared conormal image as its kernel.

The kernel consists precisely of classes of elements in I: m̄=m/I and m̄²=(m²+I)/I, so it is (I+m²)/m². This is the image part of [Stacks, Lemma 29.33.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01UZ). [Surjectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L196) checks exactness at the right; no injectivity of the separate conormal-module fiber is asserted.
Every quotient augmentation cotangent class lifts, with no flatness or smoothness.

The image of I in m/m² vanishes exactly when I⊆m², by the quotient-zero criterion in [Mathlib’s cotangent map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean#L182). Thus the defining equations have no linear term at the identity. [The field tangent criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L268) checks this infinitesimal meaning; it does not imply I=0 without further hypotheses.
Over a field the subgroup differential is onto exactly when the conormal image vanishes.

Over a field, a linear map is injective exactly when its dual is surjective, as in [Mathlib’s dual-map criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dual/Lemmas.lean#L756). Combining cotangent duality with the kernel formula gives the stated equivalence. [The surjective-coordinate-map application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L305) checks it. Infinite-dimensional cotangent spaces are allowed; no global subgroup equality is claimed.
A surjective coordinate map with onto differential has zero kernel conormal image.

Surjective f:H→K factors through its ordinary Hopf kernel quotient. Surjectivity of its differential then makes the kernel-quotient differential onto, forcing zero conormal image by [Mathlib’s dual-map criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dual/Lemmas.lean#L756) and cotangent duality. [The smooth connected subgroup comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Smooth/Dimension.lean#L59) checks its intended application with the extra global hypotheses retained.
Nested smooth connected subgroups with equal finite Lie dimension are equal; all global hypotheses remain explicit.

Rank-nullity for the surjective quotient cotangent map, with kernel equal to the conormal image, gives the displayed sum. This is the finite-dimensional consequence of [Stacks, Lemma 29.33.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01UZ). [The dual Lie-dimension formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L348) checks the correspondence. Ambient cotangent finite-dimensionality also makes the quotient and kernel finite-dimensional.
Finite cotangent rank-nullity becomes Lie dimension plus conormal image dimension equals ambient Lie dimension.

Finite-dimensional cotangent duality identifies tangent and cotangent dimensions, so rank-nullity becomes dim Lie(N)+dim N*=dim Lie(G), as in [Milne, 10.6 and Proposition 10.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=199) and [Stacks, Lemma 29.33.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01UZ). [The resulting dimension bound](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L373) checks the orientation. These are tangent dimensions; they are not identified with group dimensions without smoothness.
The exact-sequence formula bounds subgroup tangent dimension by ambient tangent dimension.

Nonnegativity of conormal dimension in the preceding exact-sequence formula gives dim Lie(N)≤dim Lie(G). This matches the tangent inclusion of [Milne, 10.14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=201). [Nested-subgroup monotonicity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L423) checks the stronger comparison. Finite ambient cotangents are explicit; disconnected and non-smooth subgroups remain allowed.
Larger defining ideals give no larger tangent dimension under finite ambient cotangents.

The attained Lie dimensions of a nonempty family lie in the finite interval 0…dim Lie(G), so one is attained maximally. This isolates the dimension-selection step used in [Milne, proof of Proposition 6.42](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=145). [The smooth connected application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Smooth/Dimension.lean#L130) checks the intended use. The family need not be finite; no greatest subgroup is asserted.
A maximal Lie-dimension member gives a minimal defining ideal when every family member is smooth and connected.

I≤J enlarges the conormal image, so subtracting its dimension in the common ambient dimension formula gives dim Lie(V(J))≤dim Lie(V(I)). This agrees with the subgroup inclusion in [Milne, 10.14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=201). [Conormal monotonicity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L101) checks the reversed ideal order, with finite ambient cotangents retaining genuine dimensions.
Ideal inclusion gives inclusion of first-order equation images in the common cotangent space.

Geometric connectedness gives irreducibility; ambient reducedness then makes H a domain. A nonzero element of I is a non-zero-divisor killed by H→H/I, so [Mathlib’s dimension-drop lemma](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/NonZeroDivisors.lean#L56) gives dim(H/I)+1≤dim H. [The smooth Lie-dimension specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Dimension.lean#L76) checks the use. The subgroup itself need not be smooth or connected.
Properness gives strict Lie-dimension drop when ambient and subgroup are smooth and the ambient group is geometrically connected.

The proper-subgroup Krull-dimension drop becomes a strict Lie-dimension inequality because both ambient group and subgroup are smooth. This matches [Milne, Proposition 10.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=202). [The smooth subgroup dimension comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Dimension.lean#L98) checks that conversion. Ambient geometric connectedness is retained; neither connectedness of the subgroup nor perfectness of the field is assumed.
Smoothness of the quotient group identifies its Krull dimension with the dimension of its embedded Lie algebra.

Smoothness gives a split conormal injection; zero identity fiber and connected target make that finite projective module vanish. The kernel becomes idempotent, and connected source plus counit force it to be zero. This realizes [Milne, Proposition 10.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=202) using [Stacks, Lemma 29.35.17](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06AA). [The subgroup-equality comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Smooth/Dimension.lean#L59) checks the application with both smoothness and connectedness hypotheses.
Nested smooth connected subgroups with equal finite Lie dimension are equal; all global hypotheses remain explicit.

The bundled object is exactly a continuous map from the closed unit interval with value x at zero and y at one. Endpoint proofs are part of the structure, so an arbitrary interval map cannot masquerade as a path between unrelated points. No separation or path-connectedness assumption on the ambient space is needed. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L60).

The topology is induced by forgetting the endpoint proofs into C(I,X) with its compact-open topology. The forgetful image is precisely the continuous maps taking zero to x and one to y, so this is the usual fixed-endpoint path space with its subspace topology. Neither a metric nor Hausdorffness of X is assumed. Compared with [Expanded Appendix §2 pp13–14, compact-open topology and Proposition A.14](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L180).

A family of fixed-endpoint paths is continuous into this path space exactly when its evaluation map on parameter × I is jointly continuous. The proof uses the induced topology and compact-open currying/evaluation. Hatcher A.14 supplies the relevant correspondence because I is locally compact; the arbitrary parameter space and target need no Hausdorff assumption. Compared with [Expanded Appendix §2 pp13–14, compact-open topology and Proposition A.14](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L185).

This instance states joint continuity of evaluation Path(x,y) × I → X. It is obtained by continuously forgetting to the compact-open continuous-map space. Hatcher A.14(a) applies since the evaluation domain I is locally compact; no local compactness or separation assumption on the target X is needed. Compared with [Expanded Appendix §2 pp13–14, compact-open topology and Proposition A.14](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L183).

The reflexive path is the constant continuous map with value x, hence has both endpoints x. Its entire image is the singleton {x}. This is the constant path used in the standard path-homotopy conventions; the declaration itself asserts neither strict concatenation identities nor any uniqueness of loops at x. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L143).

Reversal precomposes a path with t ↦ 1−t on I, swapping its source and target. Reversing twice gives the original path, and reversal preserves its image. This agrees with Hatcher’s inverse-path convention before passing to homotopy classes; it is unrelated to pointwise inversion in an algebraic target. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L153).

Concatenation traverses γ in the first half of I and γ′ in the second, using the rescalings 2t and 2t−1. Their common typed endpoint y makes the two formulas agree at the midpoint, where continuity is proved by pasting. This is Hatcher’s first-γ-then-γ′ convention, and the image is exactly the union of the two images. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L277).

Mapping a path is postcomposition with the given continuous map f; evaluation is f(γ(t)) and endpoints become f(x),f(y). This is the standard functorial operation on paths. The existing identity and composition formulas check the operation itself without imposing injectivity, surjectivity or separation assumptions. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L345).

This is the same postcomposition construction under the weaker, sufficient hypothesis that f is continuous on the image of γ. Every evaluated point lies in that image, so continuous-on composition supplies an interval path with endpoints f(x),f(y). Discontinuity of f elsewhere is irrelevant; the unrestricted version delegates to this construction. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L338).

The path is extended to a continuous real-line map by projecting time onto [0,1]. It agrees with γ on the interval and is constant at x before zero and y after one. This explicit constant extension preserves the standard interval-path data; no extension theorem for arbitrary closed subsets or special target space is involved. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L192).

Continuity of the real-line extension follows by composing the original interval path with the continuous projection onto [0,1]. Thus continuity also holds at the two transition points to the constant tails. The statement uses only the topology on X and the standard real interval; it does not assume uniform continuity or a metric target. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L202).

Jointly continuous families of composable paths remain jointly continuous after concatenation, even when their endpoints vary with the parameter. The proof pastes the two jointly continuous rescaled extensions along time 1/2; the shared endpoint b(t) gives agreement there. Individual continuity of every path would not suffice for this family statement. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L433).

Truncation evaluates the constant extension at min(max(s,t₀),t₁). For ordered interval times it follows γ between the cutoffs and waits outside; the exact general type starts at γ.extend(min(t₀,t₁)). Reversed cutoffs therefore give a constant path, not backward traversal. The source proves the endpoint formulas for arbitrary real cutoffs. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L533).

With the first cutoff fixed, the truncated path depends jointly continuously on the second real cutoff and the interval time. The proof restricts the existing three-variable continuous clipping formula. Its endpoints can vary with the cutoff, so the conclusion is continuity of evaluation into X, not a map into one fixed-endpoint path space. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L578).

A jointly continuous path family can be evaluated at a continuously varying real time after constant extension. The resulting map is continuous because time is first projected onto I and then fed into the jointly continuous family. This extends the usual evaluation principle while keeping the same fixed endpoints for each path in the family. Compared with [Expanded Appendix §2 pp13–14, compact-open topology and Proposition A.14](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L197).

A real-line function continuous on I, with prescribed endpoint values, restricts to a bundled path. Restricting to the interval subtype turns continuous-on into ordinary continuity, exactly matching the standard definition of a path. Global continuity of the real-line function is unnecessary and is not silently assumed. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L258).

The product path evaluates both input paths at the same time and pairs their values. Continuity follows in the product topology and the endpoints are the corresponding ordered pairs. The source formula and compatibility with simultaneous concatenation check this standard construction without any connectedness or separation assumptions on the factors. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L469).

Pointwise multiplication pairs the two paths and postcomposes with continuous multiplication, giving endpoints a₁*a₂ and b₁*b₂ in that order. Although the prose mentions topological groups, the exact construction needs only a multiplication operation with joint continuity. Associativity, an identity and inverses play no role in its validity. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L518).

Pointwise inversion is postcomposition with the continuous unary inverse operation. It sends γ(t) to γ(t)⁻¹ and its endpoints to a⁻¹,b⁻¹, preserving the direction of the time parameter. The topological-group wording describes a standard instance; the type correctly uses only Inv and ContinuousInv, with no inverse laws required. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L524).

The image of the constant extension on any real subset containing I is exactly the original path image. One inclusion follows because the extension introduces no new values; the other uses the included interval time representing each value of γ. The only condition on the subset is containment of the full closed interval. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L233).

The identity homomorphism makes a commutative semiring an algebra over itself, with scalar multiplication equal to its multiplication. The implementation and documentation agree, including the identity structure map. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~sharifi/notes/algebra-ch05.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Defs.lean#L385).

An algebra over a commutative semiring carries its expected module structure: r acts by multiplication by algebraMap(r). The six module laws follow from the homomorphism and semiring laws. Additive inverses are unnecessary. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~sharifi/notes/algebra-ch05.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Defs.lean#L267).

Scalar multiplication from an R-algebra commutes with left multiplication by elements of the algebra. This follows because the image of R is central. The result does not require the whole algebra to be commutative. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~sharifi/notes/algebra-ch05.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Basic.lean#L430).

MulAction gives a unital left monoid action: multiplying scalars composes their actions in the same order, and the scalar identity acts identically. Its class documentation states precisely these laws. No group inverses are needed. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/gpaction.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Defs.lean#L133).

SemigroupAction is a left semigroup action satisfying (r*s) • x = r • (s • x). It does not impose a unit law. The own documentation and field match this deliberately weaker notion. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/gpaction.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Defs.lean#L102).

DistribMulAction is a monoid action by endomorphisms of an additive monoid, preserving both addition and zero. The target need not be commutative. The docstring’s group-ring example is correctly scoped to its preceding group and abelian-group assumptions. Compared with [the reference](https://alistairsavage.ca/mat3141/notes/MAT%203141%20-%20Linear%20Algebra%20II.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean#L346).

DistribSMul requires scalar multiplication to preserve addition and zero in its target. It removes the unit and composition requirements of a monoid action. Its signature deliberately permits a raw scalar type and only AddZeroClass on the target. Compared with [the reference](https://alistairsavage.ca/mat3141/notes/MAT%203141%20-%20Linear%20Algebra%20II.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean#L270).

The MulActionWithZero docstring incorrectly calls A a monoid and refers to multiplication on A, although A only has a zero. The class itself is correct: it combines a monoid action with both zero laws. The doc should describe scalar-action associativity, (r*s) • a = r • (s • a), with multiplication in M₀. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/gpaction.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean#L185).

SMulWithZero supplies a scalar operation with zeros in both types and requires a • 0 = 0 and 0 • x = 0. It makes no unit, associativity or distributivity claim. The documentation matches those two absorption laws. Compared with [the reference](https://alistairsavage.ca/mat3141/notes/MAT%203141%20-%20Linear%20Algebra%20II.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean#L116).

SMulZeroClass is precisely a scalar operation preserving the target zero. The scalar type need not have a zero, multiplication or identity. Thus the class asserts a • 0 = 0 without asserting a separate zero-scalar law. Compared with [the reference](https://alistairsavage.ca/mat3141/notes/MAT%203141%20-%20Linear%20Algebra%20II.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean#L50).

SemilinearMapClass describes additive maps that transport scalar multiplication along the specified semiring homomorphism σ: f(c • x) = σ(c) • f(x). The source and documentation agree. Unlike the classical field-automorphism case, σ need not be invertible or injective. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/galoistheory/galoisdescent.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L107).

LinearMapClass specializes SemilinearMapClass to the identity semiring homomorphism. Its maps preserve addition and the same scalar action on source and target, as stated in the documentation. It requires no injectivity or topology. Compared with [the reference](https://alistairsavage.ca/mat3141/notes/MAT%203141%20-%20Linear%20Algebra%20II.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L121).

DistribMulActionSemiHomClass requires additive monoid homomorphisms that are φ-equivariant for the given distributive monoid actions. Its own documentation matches these conditions. The parameter φ is intentionally a plain function, not an assumed monoid homomorphism. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/galoistheory/galoisdescent.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/GroupTheory/GroupAction/Hom.lean#L639).

MulActionSemiHomClass states exactly φ-equivariance: f(c • x) = φ(c) • f(x). It requires only scalar operations, so neither scalar type need be a monoid and φ need not be a homomorphism. The own documentation makes no stronger preservation claim. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/galoistheory/galoisdescent.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/GroupTheory/GroupAction/Hom.lean#L125).

An equivariant map for two actions of the same scalar type preserves scalar multiplication. This is the defining equivariance equation with the identity scalar transport. No additive structure, monoid laws or injectivity of the map are required. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/galoistheory/galoisdescent.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/GroupTheory/GroupAction/Hom.lean#L149).

The identity scalar fixes every element in a monoid action. The theorem exposes the supplied MulAction unit law; it does not claim this for an arbitrary scalar operation. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/gpaction.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Defs.lean#L416).

Successive left actions by a₁ and a₂ equal the action by a₁*a₂. The multiplication order is correct for noncommutative monoids. The proof reverses the existing action-associativity equation. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/gpaction.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Defs.lean#L411).

Scalar multiplication distributes over target addition under DistribSMul. The theorem is exactly the defining addition-preservation law. It needs no multiplication or addition on the scalar type and no associativity or commutativity of target addition. Compared with [the reference](https://alistairsavage.ca/mat3141/notes/MAT%203141%20-%20Linear%20Algebra%20II.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean#L278).

Every scalar sends the target zero to zero under SMulZeroClass. This is the stipulated target-zero law, requiring no zero or algebraic operations on the scalar type. Compared with [the reference](https://alistairsavage.ca/mat3141/notes/MAT%203141%20-%20Linear%20Algebra%20II.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean#L59).

The zero scalar sends every target element to target zero under SMulWithZero. The scalar and target zeros have the correct distinct types. No multiplication, identity or distributivity assumption is needed. Compared with [the reference](https://alistairsavage.ca/mat3141/notes/MAT%203141%20-%20Linear%20Algebra%20II.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean#L134).
